fine_bathymetry.attribution: EMODnet Bathymetry HR-DTM HR_Lidar_Sul (EDMO 590). Not for navigation.

provenance.note: Discovered via the EMODnet Bathymetry HR-DTM WFS (emodnet:hr_bathymetry_area). The WFS publishes a product release year and no seabed stability, so both are taken from the source programme instead: the tile is 2011 DGT/APA airborne LiDAR over rocky reef. seabed_stability drives whether depth MAE may carry the accuracy claim, so it is recorded from the survey, not guessed from the release.
Southern edge reaches the shelf break off Cape Espichel, where the floor drops past 1900 m. The AOI alone only reaches ~119 m. Reproduces the prototype grid cell for cell.

metadata.screening_note: The prototype's clarity_bbox, kept verbatim. It contains the 60 CCMAR diver quadrats and the habitat_bbox, so date rankings taken over it describe the water the golden retrievals were measured in.
metadata.geometry_provenance: Taken from the lee_demo prototype's SiteProfile (kelp_observe/tools/lee_demo/sites.py), which is where the Phase 4.2 reference retrievals were produced. The wider Arrábida strip in the KelpObserve project documentation (-9.15, 38.39, -8.90, 38.51) is the field-campaign AOI and excludes every quadrat; it is not this AOI.
metadata.coarse_bathymetry_note: Bathymetric LiDAR stops at ~29 m here, so the deep-water gates (z > 30 m and z*Kd(490) > 6) need a coarser grid. The prototype used an EMODnet DTM subset; no absolute URI is recorded, so coarse_bathymetry is left unset rather than pointed at a checkout.
